glosses: Espérer.

examples.text: Ich hoffe, das Wetter bleibt weiterhin stabil.

examples.text: Nach 30 Jahren Fahndung wird die frühere Linksterroristin Daniela Klette in Berlin-Kreuzberg gefasst. Angehörige von Opfern hoffen nun auf Aufklärung.
examples.translation: Après 30 ans de recherche, l’ancienne terroriste de gauche Daniela Klette a été arrêtée à Berlin-Kreuzberg. Les proches des victimes espèrent désormais que la lumière sera faite l’affaire.

examples.text: »(...) Sein Minimum (ist) zweihundertfünfzig Dollar pro Partie.« Ich lachte. »Auf diesen Gedanken wäre ich eigentlich nie geraten, daß Figuren von Schwarz auf Weiß zu schieben ein derart einträgliches Geschäft sein kann. Nun, ich hoffe, Sie haben sich ebenso höflich empfohlen.«
examples.translation: « (...) Son minimum étant deux cent cinquante dollars la partie. » Je me mis à rire. « L’idée que déplacer des pièces d’une case blanche vers une noire puisse être une affaire aussi rentable ne me serait jamais venue à l’esprit, j’avoue. J’espère donc que vous avez pris congé avec toute la politesse qu’il mérite. »

examples.text: Und der Stadtplan versetzt sie mit seiner Zuverlässigkeit in sprachloses Staunen: Wenn er ankündigt, die zweite Straße rechts sei St. Mark’s Place, dann ist es auch St. Mark’s Place – ein Ding der Unmöglichkeit in der Sowjetunion, wo die Stadtpläne, so man denn welche findet, garantiert falsch sind; entweder, weil sie aus einer Zeit von vor dem Krieg stammen oder weil sie großen Bauarbeiten vorgreifen und die Stadt so zeigen, wie man sie in fünfzehn Jahren auszusehen hofft, oder auch aus purer Lust, den Besucher zu verwirren, denn dieser steht immer mehr oder wenig unter Spionageverdacht.
examples.translation: Quant au plan, sa fiabilité les stupéfie : s’il annonce que la seconde rue à droite est St Mark’s Place, eh bien c’est St Mark’s Place, chose inconcevable en Union soviétique où les plans de villes, quand on en trouve, sont immanquablement faux, soit parce qu’ils datent de la dernière guerre, soit parce qu’ils anticipent sur de grands travaux et montrent la cité comme on espère qu’elle sera dans quinze ans, soit par pure volonté d’égarer le visiteur, toujours plus ou moins suspect d’espionnage.

translations.source_sense_description: zuversichtlich erwarten, in die Zukunft vertrauen

glosses: To want (something) to happen, with a sense of expectation that it might [with that (+ clause); or (informal) with clause; or with so or (negative) not].

examples.text: — Is he going to shut up soon? — I hope so.
I'm going to get a new car. I hope it will be better than the last one.
They are hoping it does not rain, but I expect it will.
He's still hoping that everything will turn out fine.
I'd hoped I'd find a job, but I never did, so I was hoping you could lend me some cash.
I hope {to - (that) I'll} have finished by next Sat at the latest.
It is to be hoped that some corresponding smartening up of these other schedules may be expected before long.

The solitary, lumbering trolls of Scandinavian mythology would sometimes be turned to stone by exposure to sunlight. Barack Obama is hoping that several measures announced on June 4th will have a similarly paralysing effect on their modern incarnation, the patent troll.

glosses: To intend to do something and look forward to the prospect of having done it [with to (+ infinitive)].

examples.text: I hope to succeed.

He looked round the poor room, at the distempered walls, and the bad engravings in meretricious frames, the crinkly paper and wax flowers on the chiffonier; and he thought of a room like Father Bryan's, with panelling, with cut glass, with tulips in silver pots, such a room as he had hoped to have for his own.

glosses: To expect optimistically that one might get something (either a change in circumstance or an object) [with for].

examples.text: They're hoping for the best, but I don't think it's looking very good.
I'm hoping for my boss to offer me a pay raise.

glosses: To place confidence; to trust with confident expectation of good [with in].

examples.text: I hope in thy word.
Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? Hope thou in God.

glosses: To wish.

examples.text: I hope you all the best.

glosses: The feeling of trust, confidence, belief or expectation that something wished for can or will happen.

examples.text: All hopes for a truce are gone after the latest attack.
After losing my job, there's frail hope of affording my world cruise.
There is still hope that we can find our missing cat.

My hopes wa'n't disappointed. I never saw clams thicker than they was along them inshore flats. I filled my dreener in no time, and then it come to me that 'twouldn't be a bad idee to get a lot more, take 'em with me to Wellmouth, and peddle 'em out.

glosses: The actual thing wished for.
A person or thing that is a source of hope.

examples.text: We still have one hope left: my roommate might see the note I left on the table.

glosses: The virtuous desire for future good.

examples.text: But now abideth faith, hope, love, these three; and the greatest of these is love.

glosses: A hollow; a valley, especially the upper end of a narrow mountain valley when it is nearly encircled by smooth, green slopes; a combe.
A sloping plain between mountain ridges.
A small bay; an inlet; a haven.

examples.text: Being by contrarie winds driuen to staie against Erith, at Grauesend, in Tilberie hope.
A little hamlet which straggled along the side of a creek formed by the discharge of a small brook into the sea[…]It was called Wolf's Hope (i.e. Wolf's Haven).

glosses: Confidence in or reliance on some person or quality.

examples.text: He needs to regain her trust if he is ever going to win her back.
to lose trust in someone
build up trust
a relationship built on mutual trust
taking things upon trust.
O ever-failing trust / In mortal strength!

glosses: Dependence upon something in the future; hope.

examples.text: Such trust have we through Christ.

glosses: Confidence in the future payment for goods or services supplied; credit.

examples.text: I was out of cash, but the landlady let me have it on trust.

glosses: That which is committed or entrusted; something received in confidence; a charge.
That upon which confidence is reposed; ground of reliance; hope.

examples.text: O Lord God, thou art my trust from my youth.

glosses: Trustworthiness, reliability.
The condition or obligation of one to whom anything is confided; responsible charge or office.

examples.text:
I do profess to be no less than I seem; to serve him truly that
will put me in trust

17th century, John Denham, Of Justice
Reward them well, if they observe their trust.

glosses: The confidence vested in a person who has legal ownership of a property to manage for the benefit of another.

examples.text: I put the house into my sister's trust.

glosses: An arrangement whereby property or money is given to be held by a third party (a trustee), on the basis that it will be managed for the benefit of, or eventually transferred to, a stated beneficiary; for example, money to be given to a child when he or she reaches adulthood.
A group of businessmen or traders organised for mutual benefit to produce and distribute specific commodities or services, and managed by a central body of trustees.
Affirmation of the access rights of a user of a computer system.
To place confidence in, to rely on, to confide in.

examples.text: He that trusts without reserve will at last be deceived.
We cannot trust anyone who deceives us.
If I live to see it, I will never trust his word after.

glosses: To have faith in; to rely on for continuing support or aid.

examples.text: In God We Trust
Trust in me, just in me / Shut your eyes and trust in me

glosses: To give credence to; to believe; to credit.

examples.text: Trust me, you looke well.

glosses: To hope confidently; to believe (usually with a phrase or infinitive clause as the object)

examples.text: I trust you have cleaned your room?
I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face.
We trust we have a good conscience.

glosses: to show confidence in a person by entrusting them with something.

examples.text: Whom, with your power and fortune, sir, you trust, Now to suspect is vain.

glosses: To commit, as to one's care; to entrust.

examples.text: Merchants were not willing to trust precious cargoes to any custody but that of a man-of-war.

glosses: To give credit to; to sell to upon credit, or in confidence of future payment.

examples.text: Merchants and manufacturers trust their customers annually with goods.

glosses: To rely on (something), as though having trust (on it).

examples.text: to trust to luck
Having lost the book, he had to trust to his memory for further details.

glosses: To risk; to venture confidently.

examples.text: [Beguiled] by thee to trust thee from my side.

glosses: To have trust; to be credulous; to be won to confidence; to confide.

examples.text: More ſhould I queſtion thee, and more I muſt, / Though more to know, could not be more to truſt: […]
I will trust and not be afraid.

glosses: To sell or deliver anything in reliance upon a promise of payment; to give credit.
Ellipsis of trust me.

examples.text: You'll get your money back bro, trust.
P.S. Capitalizing MINORITY really doesn't help your cause bruh. Trust.

glosses: Secure, safe.
Faithful, dependable.
of or relating to a trust.

glosses: Attendre.

examples.text:
Duchotel. — Est-il pressé !
Cassagne.— Pardon, espère un moment, espère.
Duchotel, qui ne comprend pas. — Quoi ?
Cassagne, passant devant lui et allant à Moricet. — Espère un peu !

glosses: ou (Louisiane) et (Poitevin-Saintongeais) Attendre la venue de quelqu’un.

examples.text: Peut-être Janine appartient-elle à cette race qu’un vieil avocat connaît bien : ces femmes chez qui l’espérance est une maladie, qui ne guérissent pas d’espérer, et qui, après vingt ans, regardent encore la porte avec des yeux de bête fidèle.
Nous vous espérons demain à la maison pour le dîner.

– Qu’est-ce que tu fais là ?
– J’attends Nougaro…
– En Afrique, on ne dit pas qu’on attend quelqu’un, on dit qu’on l’espère !...
– Alors je suis en train d’espérer Nougaro …

glosses: Attendre les bienfaits divins.

examples.text: Vivre comme un dieu exige que l’on cesse de croire aux dieux. Ainsi, la leçon des épicuriens est que la philosophie change les hommes en dieux en leur enseignant qu’il n'y a pas sur cette terre d’autres dieux qu’eux-mêmes dès lors qu’ils auront cessé de croire et vainement d’espérer.

glosses: Considérer l’objet de son souhait comme réalisable.

examples.text: Un mémoire que je publierai prochainement ne laissera plus, je l’espère, aucune incertitude dans l’esprit de tous les archéologues de bonne foi.
[…], où il ne restait que les gardes municipaux et des pompiers travaillant à circonscrire l’incendie qu'ils n’espéraient plus éteindre.
Les différentes dévaluations, dont la dernière en vigueur datait du 8 juin 1306, étaient loin de lui avoir rapporté ce qu’il en avait espéré.
Comme dans les prépas scientifiques, il est tout à fait possible de la redoubler (on dit « cuber ») en espérant être accepté dans une école plus prestigieuse.
Vers 2 heures du matin, je parviens à quitter la soirée. J’ai passé mon temps à ignorer au maximum Elias […]. J’ai aussi laissé Gabriel me draguer en espérant que ça fasse les pieds au premier.
